content: Oral cabotegravir, when combined with rilpivirine, is approved as a complete regimen for the short-term treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults who are virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) on a stable antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen. These individuals must have no history of treatment failure and no known or suspected resistance to either cabotegravir or rilpivirine. Prior to initiating pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), a negative HIV-1 test is required. The safety and efficacy of cabotegravir in adolescents weighing less than 35 kg have not been established. A negative HIV-1 test is mandatory before starting PrEP. Cabotegravir is metabolized by UGT1A1 and UGT1A9 enzymes. Strong inducers of these enzymes, such as apalutamide, carbamazepine, desogestrel, lamotrigine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone, and rifampin, significantly increase cabotegravir metabolism, leading to reduced systemic exposure and a higher risk of virologic failure. These drugs are contraindicated with cabotegravir. Rifabutin can decrease cabotegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. While rifabutin may be co-administered with oral cabotegravir, it is contraindicated with the extended-release injectable suspension Cabenuva (cabotegravir and rilpivirine). Antiretroviral medications, including cabotegravir, may interfere with the manufacturing of gene therapy products such as atidarsagene autotemcel, betibeglogene autotemcel, elivaldogene autotemcel, and lovotibeglogene autotemcel. Patients should discontinue ARTs at least one month before cell mobilization or the expected duration for medication elimination and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period. Cation-containing products, such as aluminum hydroxide, magnesium carbonate, magnesium trisilicate, calcium carbonate, calcium/vitamin D, magnesium chloride, magnesium citrate, magnesium hydroxide, magnesium oxide, and zinc, can reduce cabotegravir levels by binding to it in the gastrointestinal tract. To mitigate this interaction, antacid products should be administered at least two hours before or four hours after taking oral cabotegravir. Ublituximab may reduce the effectiveness of cabotegravir due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Close monitoring and therapy modification are recommended. In summary, cabotegravir's interactions with enzyme inducers, cation-containing products, and immunosuppressive agents require careful consideration to avoid reduced efficacy and virologic failure.
